caveats: Each cell was run once, so there are no confidence intervals; differences under 3% should be treated as noise.
Going from 65k·c16k to 256k·c16k changes the context (65k to 256k) and the radix/prefix cache (off to on) at the same time, so it is not a one-factor comparison.

The older configs (vLLM 65k, mem 0.88, 65k·c8k) ran on different nodes; TTFT, TPOT, ITL and E2E on the dashboard are recomputed from each run's per-request export and can differ from the diary tables (which hold the older mean/median numbers).
SGLang MTP at c64 runs only 32 concurrent slots (vLLM runs all 64).

Why MTP shows a higher ITL than base: ITL here is the inter-chunk latency (the dashboard offers avg/p50/p90/p95/p99/max, the example below is the mean), i.e. the gap between streamed response chunks. With MTP each verify step emits several tokens in one chunk (raw export of the 256k·c8k c1 high-entropy cell: base 1.00 tokens/chunk, 1020.7 chunks per request, ITL 14.3 ms; MTP 2.31 tokens/chunk, 442.5 chunks per request, ITL 17.9 ms), so ITL is the time of one draft+verify step, which is longer than a base decode step. TPOT, (e2e - TTFT) / (OSL - 1), divides by tokens and is 7.7 ms for MTP versus 14.3 ms for base. Compare MTP against base with TPOT, E2E or throughput, not ITL.

The serve commands in the tooltips are reconstructed from the recipes (body scripts at the matching commits) and were checked against server_args in the logs of the 256k·c8k config; the older configs were not checked against logs. $PORT is assigned by the launcher.
